summary.en: Nicolás Maduro and his wife have again pleaded not guilty to U.S. conspiracy to torture charges in New York, while the United States has lifted sanctions on Jorge Rodríguez, head of Venezuela's National Assembly. The U.S. Space Force has deployed electromagnetic and electronic warfare systems against Venezuela, mirroring actions taken in Iran. EnergyNow reports that global shipping disruptions and Venezuelan supply pressure have widened the Alberta heavy oil discount to over $25 per barrel. In Chile, a Venezuelan gang member received a 20-year sentence for kidnapping and killing a dissident. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Nicolás Maduro og hans kone har igjen erklært seg uskyldige i anklager om konspirasjon til tortur i USA i New York, mens USA har opphevet sanksjoner mot Jorge Rodríguez, lederen for Venezuelas nasjonalforsamling. US Space Force har satt i drift elektromagnetiske og elektroniske krigssystemer mot Venezuela, i likhet med tiltak som ble gjort mot Iran. EnergyNow rapporterer at globale forstyrrelser i skipsfarten og press på venezuelanske leveranser har økt Alberta-rabatten på tungolje til over 25 dollar per fat. I Chile fikk et venezuelansk gjengmedlem 20 års fengsel for kidnapping og drap på en dissident. To dødsfall i kamp ble registrert i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
